chapter: Other drummers and New Orleans musicians
title: Frog's brother Ferdinand and playing with George Lewis
summary: Dick Allen addresses another visitor, Frog, about his brother Ferdinand and his work with George Lewis at Bourbon Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Let me ask Frog about something. Did you get anything about his brother, Ferdinand? Not so much. Who is your brother Ferdinand? I wanted to know more about him. You mentioned him once. Well, I can tell you. I know he made this record with Papa, my Joan of Fiend. He made it up the On Canal Street at the Decker deal. Well, he can tell you more about it.
We have his address, we'll try to talk to him.

Yeah, and he's saying... Well, when you do, let me make an appointment with him, you know. Yeah, well that would be a good one. So you'll be sure to get him, you know. Yeah, I do that. And did you ask him anything about the El Morocco?
The club up here, you know? Mm-hmm.

Well, Bourbon Street? Yeah. I worked there with George. He played with all of you. Oh, wow. Only a few nights. What style were you playing before you went with George? Commercial music, anything come up. Anything? Reading? I've done everything in music but play a parade or funeral. I wasn't. I wasn't ill. Mm-hmm. Well, definitely reading, that's for sure. I see. Yeah. Did you play any of the old New Orleans style music before you got with George? We used to do it. With Freddie Band before we got on the street. Oh, yeah, I see. But not as many tunes but we used to do it now. Mm-hmm. Before this music got back, you know? Mm-hmm. I see. Yeah, I have just a couple of things I wanted to ask him about when I was at home. Uh, back to Chester. I did think of one thing I didn't ask you. Who were some of your favorite clarinet players, I'd say, when you were quite young going around?
